SMTO-CFG-0052 — SMTO needs a maximum database row count above zero

GUID: 9fee5f26-f79a-406c-9fcd-08610d5539f8
Slug: config-database-max-rows-must-be-greater-than
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO rejected a maximum database row count of zero or less. If you were saving a user's settings, nothing was saved; if SMTO was starting, it stopped before opening your data.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you saw this on the Users page, select Manage for that user, open Additional configuration, and set Maximum database rows above zero, or clear the box. The box accepts 0, but SMTO needs room for at least one row to return any database results.
  2. Select Save user. The corrected value applies only after you save; an empty box uses the installation's value.
  3. If a user's workspace won't open with this error, an administrator should correct that user's Maximum database rows on the Users page, as in steps 1 and 2. Each workspace starts with its user's saved limits, so one bad saved value blocks it.
  4. If SMTO stopped while starting, find AOR_DATABASE_MAX_ROWS where SMTO is started, delete it (usual value 1000) or set it above zero, then start SMTO again from there. At startup this limit comes only from that setting.

What success looks like

  • The Users page shows Account updated, or the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other limits on the Users page, such as Model temperature or Model timeout, to get past this error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected database_max_rows (environment variable AOR_DATABASE_MAX_ROWS at startup, or a per-user configuration override) because it is zero or negative.

What this means

  • database_max_rows is zero or negative during application settings validation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • database_max_rows is zero or negative during application settings validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the maximum result-row setting, distinct from a query's chosen default.

How to fix it

  • For a per-user override, set the user's database_max_rows (Users > Manage > Additional configuration > Maximum database rows) to a positive integer or remove it; WorkspaceManager.validate_changes rejects the save and user_settings rejects an already-saved bad value when that workspace starts. For startup, unset AOR_DATABASE_MAX_ROWS or set it to a positive integer (default 1000) and restart the Server.
  • Set database_max_rows to a supported positive row count.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported positive database result ceiling validates.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
